KD-01.ht:
1) Setup: Feet hip-width, knees soft, load in front of the thighs; flat back, shoulders back. Equipment: Dowel.
2) Execution: Push the hips back and hinge the trunk forward; the load stays close to the legs, hamstrings lengthen, back stays flat.
3) Return / finish: Drive the hips forward and squeeze the glutes to stand tall; do not lean back from the lower back.
4) Tempo and breathing: Controlled lowering, powerful and determined push / pull. (Tempo: 2-1-1.) Breathe out in the effort, in on the return; do not hold your breath for long.
5) Dose: 1-2 x 6-10 · BW – band · rest: 30 s.
6) Common mistakes: Rounding the back, bending the knees too much (turning it into a squat), load drifting away from the legs, leaning back at the top.
7) Regress: Shorten the range (just below the knee), learn the hinge with a dowel on the back. Progress: Increase load, go single-leg or lower in 3-4 s.

KD-13.ht:
1) Setup: Kettlebell in front of the feet, hip-hinge position, arms straight. Equipment: Kettlebell.
2) Execution: Hike the bell between the legs, then snap the hips to float it to chest height (arms only guide).
3) Return / finish: Receive the bell with a hip hinge on the way down and keep the rhythm.
4) Tempo and breathing: Move at maximal speed, explosively; short ground contact. Every rep high quality, no accumulated fatigue. Breathe out in the effort, in on the return; do not hold your breath for long.
5) Dose: 3-5 x 3-5 · %30-60 1RM / BW · rest: 2-3 min.
6) Common mistakes: Squatting the swing, lifting with the arms, leaning back at the top.
7) Regress: Start with a light bell, hip hinge and deadlift. Progress: Heavier bell or single-arm swing.

2) Execution: Drive through the heels and lift the hips until trunk and thighs form a straight line; squeeze the glutes.
3) Return / finish: Lower under control; do not arch the lower back.
4) Tempo and breathing: Controlled lowering, powerful and determined push / pull. Breathe out in the effort, in on the return; do not hold your breath for long.

6) Common mistakes: Lifting from the lower back, not squeezing the glutes, knees opening / collapsing.
7) Regress: Reduce range, use both legs. Progress: Single leg, add load or hold 3 s at the top.

KD-23.ht:
1) Setup: Heels fixed (partner / machine / strap), hips extended. Equipment: Nordic station / partner. Keep the straps taut; body angle sets the difficulty (more upright = easier).
2) Execution: Bend the knee with the hamstrings (curl) or lower the trunk slowly forward (Nordic).
3) Return / finish: Make the eccentric part slow (3-5 s); do not bend at the hips.
4) Tempo and breathing: The lowering (lengthening) phase is slow and controlled; the return can be assisted or fast. Breathe out in the effort, in on the return; do not hold your breath for long.
5) Dose: 2-3 x 3-6 · BW / submaximal · rest: 2 min.
6) Common mistakes: Bending at the hips, fast eccentric, arching the lower back.
7) Regress: Shorten the range, use band assistance. Progress: Longer eccentric, single leg or larger range.

KD-78.ht:
1) Setup: Kettlebell in front of the feet, hip-hinge position, arms straight. Equipment: Dumbbell.
2) Execution: Hike the bell between the legs, then snap the hips to float it to chest height (arms only guide).
3) Return / finish: Receive the bell with a hip hinge on the way down and keep the rhythm.
4) Tempo and breathing: Move at maximal speed, explosively; short ground contact. Every rep high quality, no accumulated fatigue. Breathe out in the effort, in on the return; do not hold your breath for long.
5) Dose: 3-5 x 3-5 · %30-60 1RM / BW · rest: 2-3 min.
6) Common mistakes: Squatting the swing, lifting with the arms, leaning back at the top.
7) Regress: Start with a light bell, hip hinge and deadlift. Progress: Heavier bell or single-arm swing.

3) Return / finish: Drive the hips forward and squeeze the glutes to stand tall; do not lean back from the lower back. Equal reps on each leg / arm; start with the weaker side.
4) Tempo and breathing: Controlled lowering, powerful and determined push / pull. (Tempo: 3-0-1.) Breathe out in the effort, in on the return; do not hold your breath for long.
5) Dose: 3-4 x 6-8 · %79-85 1RM · rest: 1.5-2 min.
6) Common mistakes: Rounding the back, bending the knees too much (turning it into a squat), load drifting away from the legs, leaning back at the top.
7) Regress: Shorten the range (just below the knee), learn the hinge with a dowel on the back. Progress: Increase load, go single-leg or lower in 3-4 s.

7) Regress: Shorten the range, use band assistance. Progress: Longer eccentric, single leg or larger range.

KD-157.ht:
1) Setup: On a machine or in an isometric position, back supported. Equipment: Hiperekstansiyon sehpası. Work on one leg; keep the pelvis level and the stance knee over the toes. Hold the position at the given angle; keep the force for the whole duration.
2) Execution: Extend the knee under control and hold 1 s at the top.
3) Return / finish: Lower slowly. Equal reps on each leg / arm; start with the weaker side.
4) Tempo and breathing: Position stays still; keep the force for the whole duration. Breathe rhythmically throughout; do not hold your breath.
5) Dose: 3 x 20-30 s · Pain ≤3/10 · rest: 60-90 s.
6) Common mistakes: Hips lifting off the seat, dropping the load, working in a painful range.
7) Regress: Reduce load, limit range to pain-free. Progress: Hold 2-3 s at the top, longer eccentric or single leg.

KD-158.ht:
1) Setup: Feet hip-width, knees soft, load in front of the thighs; flat back, shoulders back. Equipment: Dumbbell. Work on one leg; keep the pelvis level and the stance knee over the toes. Make the lowering (eccentric) phase slow (3-5 s).
2) Execution: Push the hips back and hinge the trunk forward; the load stays close to the legs, hamstrings lengthen, back stays flat.
3) Return / finish: Drive the hips forward and squeeze the glutes to stand tall; do not lean back from the lower back. Equal reps on each leg / arm; start with the weaker side.
4) Tempo and breathing: The lowering (lengthening) phase is slow and controlled; the return can be assisted or fast. Breathe out in the effort, in on the return; do not hold your breath for long.
5) Dose: 3 x 6 · Eksantrik 3-5 s · rest: 90 s.
6) Common mistakes: Rounding the back, bending the knees too much (turning it into a squat), load drifting away from the legs, leaning back at the top.
7) Regress: Shorten the range (just below the knee), learn the hinge with a dowel on the back. Progress: Increase load, go single-leg or lower in 3-4 s.

KD-159.ht:
1) Setup: Lie on your back or with the upper back on a bench, feet on the floor, knees about 90°. Equipment: Bodyweight.
2) Execution: Drive through the heels and lift the hips until trunk and thighs form a straight line; squeeze the glutes.
3) Return / finish: Lower under control; do not arch the lower back.
4) Tempo and breathing: Move at maximal speed, explosively; short ground contact. Every rep high quality, no accumulated fatigue. Breathe out in the effort, in on the return; do not hold your breath for long.
5) Dose: 3 x 10-20 · BW – maximal · rest: 90-120 s.
6) Common mistakes: Lifting from the lower back, not squeezing the glutes, knees opening / collapsing.
7) Regress: Reduce range, use both legs. Progress: Single leg, add load or hold 3 s at the top.

KD-160.ht:
1) Setup: Prepare the equipment (Bodyweight) so that transitions between movements are short.
2) Bacak savurma: Perform the movement from the correct start position, through full range and under control.
3) Hamstring yakalama (hızlı fren): Perform the movement from the correct start position, through full range and under control.
4) Transition: Move to the next movement within a few seconds; every part at maximal quality. Equal reps on each leg / arm; start with the weaker side.
5) Dose: 3 x 8 / side · Eksantrik 3-5 s · rest: 90 s. Stop the set if technique breaks.
6) Common mistakes: Pausing in the transition, doing the second movement poorly because of fatigue. Rushing, not reaching full range.
7) Regress: Do the movements separately. Progress: More reps or speed.

KD-161.ht:
1) Setup: Take the start position (standing / falling / from the ground). Equipment: Cable. Set the cable pulley at the right height; start with the cable taut.
2) Execution: On the cue run at maximal speed: short powerful first steps, trunk forward, active arms.
3) Return / finish: Decelerate progressively after the distance; full rest between reps. Equal reps on each leg / arm; start with the weaker side.
4) Tempo and breathing: Controlled lowering, powerful and determined push / pull. (Tempo: 2-0-1.) Breathe out in the effort, in on the return; do not hold your breath for long.
5) Dose: 3 x 10 · RPE 7-8 · rest: 90 s.
6) Common mistakes: Hips lifting off the seat, dropping the load, working in a painful range.
7) Regress: Reduce load, limit range to pain-free. Progress: Hold 2-3 s at the top, longer eccentric or single leg.

KD-162.ht:

5) Dose: 2 x 5 · Eksantrik 3-5 s · rest: 90 s. Stop the set if technique breaks.

KD-165.ht:

DD-01.ht:
1) Setup: Feet shoulder-width apart, toes slightly out; load in a safe position, chest up, trunk braced. Equipment: TRX / direk.
2) Execution: Send the hips back and down, knees tracking over the toes, and descend until the thighs are parallel (or to the lowest controlled position).
3) Return / finish: Drive the whole foot into the floor and extend hips and knees together to return to the start.
4) Tempo and breathing: Controlled lowering, powerful and determined push / pull. (Tempo: 2-1-1.) Breathe out in the effort, in on the return; do not hold your breath for long.
5) Dose: 1-2 x 6-10 · BW – band · rest: 30 s.
6) Common mistakes: Knees caving in, heels lifting, lower back rounding at the bottom, chest dropping.
7) Regress: Squat to a box or use a goblet position, reduce depth. Progress: Increase load, pause 2 s at the bottom or use a tempo squat (3 s down).

2) Execution: Send the hips back and down, knees tracking over the toes, and descend until the thighs are parallel (or to the lowest controlled position).
3) Return / finish: Drive the whole foot into the floor and extend hips and knees together to return to the start. Equal reps on each leg / arm; start with the weaker side.
4) Tempo and breathing: Controlled lowering, powerful and determined push / pull. (Tempo: 3-0-1.) Breathe out in the effort, in on the return; do not hold your breath for long.
5) Dose: 3-4 x 6-8 · %79-85 1RM · rest: 1.5-2 min.
6) Common mistakes: Knees caving in, heels lifting, lower back rounding at the bottom, chest dropping.
7) Regress: Squat to a box or use a goblet position, reduce depth. Progress: Increase load, pause 2 s at the bottom or use a tempo squat (3 s down).

1) Setup: Adjust the equipment to your body (seat height, belt speed etc.); warm up 3-5 min easy. Equipment: Barbell.
2) Execution: Work rhythmically for the given time and intensity; pain must stay ≤3/10.
3) Return / finish: Cool down by reducing intensity over the last 2-3 min. Equal reps on each leg / arm; start with the weaker side.
4) Tempo and breathing: Rhythmic and controlled; start at a conversational pace and build up. (Tempo: 3-0-1.) Breathe out in the effort, in on the return; do not hold your breath for long.

6) Common mistakes: Wrong equipment setup, increasing time despite pain, high intensity without warm-up.
7) Regress: Reduce time or resistance, use intervals (e.g. 1 min work – 1 min easy). Progress: Progressively increase time, resistance or interval intensity.

Drive the whole foot into the floor and extend hips and knees together to return to the start.
4) Transition: Move to the next movement within a few seconds; every part at maximal quality.
5) Dose: 3 x 10 steps / direction · BW · rest: 30 s. Stop the set if technique breaks.
6) Common mistakes: Pausing in the transition, doing the second movement poorly because of fatigue. Trunk leaning sideways, pelvis rotating forward, moving too fast.
7) Regress: Do the movements separately. Progress: Move the band to the knees / ankles, increase time or reps.

DD-172.ht:
1) Setup: Feet shoulder-width apart, toes slightly out; load in a safe position, chest up, trunk braced. Equipment: Band. Start by reacting to the coach's signal (sound / hand / colour).
2) Execution: Send the hips back and down, knees tracking over the toes, and descend until the thighs are parallel (or to the lowest controlled position).
3) Return / finish: Drive the whole foot into the floor and extend hips and knees together to return to the start. Equal reps on each leg / arm; start with the weaker side.
4) Tempo and breathing: Controlled lowering, powerful and determined push / pull. (Tempo: 2-0-1.) Breathe out in the effort, in on the return; do not hold your breath for long.
5) Dose: 3 x 10 · RPE 7-8 · rest: 90 s.
6) Common mistakes: Knees caving in, heels lifting, lower back rounding at the bottom, chest dropping.
7) Regress: Squat to a box or use a goblet position, reduce depth. Progress: Increase load, pause 2 s at the bottom or use a tempo squat (3 s down).

DD-173.ht:
1) Setup: On a machine or in an isometric position, back supported. Equipment: Mat.
2) Execution: Extend the knee under control and hold 1 s at the top.
3) Return / finish: Lower slowly.
4) Tempo and breathing: The lowering (lengthening) phase is slow and controlled; the return can be assisted or fast. Breathe out in the effort, in on the return; do not hold your breath for long.
5) Dose: 3 x 6-8 · Eksantrik 3-5 s · rest: 90 s.
6) Common mistakes: Hips lifting off the seat, dropping the load, working in a painful range.
7) Regress: Reduce load, limit range to pain-free. Progress: Hold 2-3 s at the top, longer eccentric or single leg.

DD-175.ht:
1) Setup: Take the start position for the exercise; trunk tall and braced, joints neutral. Equipment: Cable. Make the lowering (eccentric) phase slow (3-5 s). Set the cable pulley at the right height; start with the cable taut.
2) Execution: Perform the movement under control and through full range.
3) Return / finish: Return to the start under control and prepare for the next rep. Equal reps on each leg / arm; start with the weaker side.

DD-176.ht:
1) Setup: Stand tall; load in the hands or on the shoulders, trunk upright. Equipment: Bodyweight / DB. Rotation starts from the hips; feet push the floor, trunk and arms follow the hips.
2) Execution: Step (forward / back / sideways) and lower under control until the front knee is about 90°, knee over the toes.
3) Return / finish: Push through the front foot back to the start; equal reps on each leg. Equal reps on each leg / arm; start with the weaker side.
4) Tempo and breathing: Controlled lowering, powerful and determined push / pull. (Tempo: 2-0-1.) Breathe out in the effort, in on the return; do not hold your breath for long.
5) Dose: 3 x 6-8 / side · RPE 7-8 · rest: 90 s.
6) Common mistakes: Front knee caving in, trunk falling forward, step too short so the heel lifts, back knee hitting the floor.
7) Regress: Static split squat, one hand on the wall for support. Progress: Increase load, elevate the rear foot (Bulgarian) or go walking.

DD-177.t: Safety bar banded speed box squat
DD-177.ht:
1) Setup: Feet shoulder-width apart, toes slightly out; load in a safe position, chest up, trunk braced. Equipment: Safety bar + band + box. Set the band tension at the start; the band increases resistance in the hardest part. Box / bench must be stable and non-slip; choose the height by level.
2) Execution: Send the hips back and down, knees tracking over the toes, and descend until the thighs are parallel (or to the lowest controlled position).
3) Return / finish: Drive the whole foot into the floor and extend hips and knees together to return to the start.
4) Tempo and breathing: Move at maximal speed, explosively; short ground contact. Every rep high quality, no accumulated fatigue. Breathe out in the effort, in on the return; do not hold your breath for long.
5) Dose: 6-8 x 2 · %30-60 1RM / maximal · rest: 2-3 min.
6) Common mistakes: Knees caving in, heels lifting, lower back rounding at the bottom, chest dropping.
7) Regress: Squat to a box or use a goblet position, reduce depth. Progress: Increase load, pause 2 s at the bottom or use a tempo squat (3 s down).

AB-47.ht:

5) Dose: 2-3 x 10-15 · Light · rest: 45-60 s.

7) Regress: Start from the hang with a light load; teach with jump shrug / high pull. Progress: Start from the floor, increase load or use a complex (clean + front squat + jerk).

Drive the hips forward and squeeze the glutes to stand tall; do not lean back from the lower back.
3) Overhead press: Standing or kneeling, load at shoulder height, trunk braced. Press the load overhead until the arms are straight. Lower to the shoulders under control; do not arch the lower back.
4) Transition: Move to the next movement within a few seconds; every part at maximal quality. Equal reps on each leg / arm; start with the weaker side.

1) Setup: Prepare the equipment (Kettlebell) so that transitions between movements are short.
2) Kettlebell swing: Kettlebell in front of the feet, hip-hinge position, arms straight. Hike the bell between the legs, then snap the hips to float it to chest height (arms only guide). Receive the bell with a hip hinge on the way down and keep the rhythm.
3) Reverse lunge: Stand tall; load in the hands or on the shoulders, trunk upright. Step (forward / back / sideways) and lower under control until the front knee is about 90°, knee over the toes. Push through the front foot back to the start; equal reps on each leg.
4) Press: Perform the movement from the correct start position, through full range and under control.
5) Transition: Move to the next movement within a few seconds; every part at maximal quality. Equal reps on each leg / arm; start with the weaker side.
6) Dose: 3 x 5 / side · %30-60 1RM / maximal · rest: 2-3 min. Stop the set if technique breaks.
7) Common mistakes: Pausing in the transition, doing the second movement poorly because of fatigue.
8) Regress: Do the movements separately. Progress: Increase load or add a third movement.

KMB-221.ht:
1) Setup: Prepare the equipment (Trap bar + box) so that transitions between movements are short.
2) Trap bar deadlift: Feet hip-width, knees soft, load in front of the thighs; flat back, shoulders back. Push the hips back and hinge the trunk forward; the load stays close to the legs, hamstrings lengthen, back stays flat. Drive the hips forward and squeeze the glutes to stand tall; do not lean back from the lower back.
3) Farmer carry: Pick up the loads and stand tall. Walk the given distance with short, controlled steps; trunk does not lean. Put the loads down with bent knees.
4) Box jump triplet: Athletic stance, feet hip-width. Jump maximally with a fast countermovement; hips-knees-ankles fully extend. Land softly on the balls of the feet, knees over the toes; stick 2 s if required.
5) Transition: Move to the next movement within a few seconds; every part at maximal quality.
6) Dose: 3-4 x (3 + 20 m + 3) · %30-60 1RM / maximal · rest: 2-3 min. Stop the set if technique breaks.
7) Common mistakes: Pausing in the transition, doing the second movement poorly because of fatigue. Rounding the back, bending the knees too much (turning it into a squat), load drifting away from the legs, leaning back at the top.
8) Regress: Do the movements separately. Progress: Increase load, go single-leg or lower in 3-4 s.

KMB-222.t: Sled push to overhead med ball throw to sprint
KMB-222.ht:
1) Setup: Prepare the equipment (Sled + med ball (3 kg)) so that transitions between movements are short.
2) Sled push: Push the sled handles, trunk at 45°, arms long. Drive the sled with short powerful steps; foot lands under the hips, knee forward. Finish the distance, rest fully.
3) Overhead med ball throw: Ball at the chest / hip / overhead, athletic stance. Start from the legs and transfer force through hips and trunk to throw the ball as fast as possible. Catch or retrieve the ball; every rep at maximal speed.
4) Sprint: Take the start position (standing / falling / from the ground). On the cue run at maximal speed: short powerful first steps, trunk forward, active arms. Decelerate progressively after the distance; full rest between reps.
5) Transition: Move to the next movement within a few seconds; every part at maximal quality.
6) Dose: 4 x 1 round · BW – maximal · rest: 90-120 s. Stop the set if technique breaks.
7) Common mistakes: Pausing in the transition, doing the second movement poorly because of fatigue.
8) Regress: Do the movements separately. Progress: Increase load or add a third movement.

KMB-223.dn: Off-season · Pre-season · In-season (low volume) · International break
KMB-223.ht:
1) Setup: Prepare the equipment (Barbell (dirsek içinde)) so that transitions between movements are short.
2) Zercher squat: Feet shoulder-width apart, toes slightly out; load in a safe position, chest up, trunk braced. Send the hips back and down, knees tracking over the toes, and descend until the thighs are parallel (or to the lowest controlled position). Drive the whole foot into the floor and extend hips and knees together to return to the start.
3) Zercher carry: Pick up the loads and stand tall. Walk the given distance with short, controlled steps; trunk does not lean. Put the loads down with bent knees.
4) Transition: Move to the next movement within a few seconds; every part at maximal quality.
5) Dose: 3-4 x (4 + 20 m) · %80-90 1RM · rest: 2-3 min. Stop the set if technique breaks.
6) Common mistakes: Pausing in the transition, doing the second movement poorly because of fatigue. Knees caving in, heels lifting, lower back rounding at the bottom, chest dropping.
7) Regress: Do the movements separately. Progress: Increase load, pause 2 s at the bottom or use a tempo squat (3 s down).

KMB-224.t: Offset KB reverse lunge to single-arm press
KMB-224.ht:
1) Setup: Prepare the equipment (Kettlebell (12-20 kg)) so that transitions between movements are short.
2) Offset KB reverse lunge: Stand tall; load in the hands or on the shoulders, trunk upright. Step (forward / back / sideways) and lower under control until the front knee is about 90°, knee over the toes. Push through the front foot back to the start; equal reps on each leg.
3) Single-arm press: Standing or kneeling, load at shoulder height, trunk braced. Press the load overhead until the arms are straight. Lower to the shoulders under control; do not arch the lower back.
4) Transition: Move to the next movement within a few seconds; every part at maximal quality. Equal reps on each leg / arm; start with the weaker side.
5) Dose: 3 x 6 / side · RPE 7-8 · rest: 90 s. Stop the set if technique breaks.
6) Common mistakes: Pausing in the transition, doing the second movement poorly because of fatigue. Front knee caving in, trunk falling forward, step too short so the heel lifts, back knee hitting the floor.
7) Regress: Do the movements separately. Progress: Increase load, elevate the rear foot (Bulgarian) or go walking.

KMB-225.t: Snatch-grip high pull to overhead squat
KMB-225.ht:
1) Setup: Prepare the equipment (Barbell (wide grip)) so that transitions between movements are short.
2) Snatch-grip high pull: Bar / dumbbells at mid-thigh or from the floor; arms straight, back flat. Extend hips-knees-ankles explosively, shrug, raise the load and drop under to catch if required. Lower the load under control; reduce the load if technique breaks.
3) Overhead squat: Feet shoulder-width apart, toes slightly out; load in a safe position, chest up, trunk braced. Send the hips back and down, knees tracking over the toes, and descend until the thighs are parallel (or to the lowest controlled position). Drive the whole foot into the floor and extend hips and knees together to return to the start.
4) Transition: Move to the next movement within a few seconds; every part at maximal quality.
5) Dose: 4 x (3 + 2) · %60-80 1RM · rest: 2-3 min. Stop the set if technique breaks.
6) Common mistakes: Pausing in the transition, doing the second movement poorly because of fatigue. Pulling the bar with the arms, bar drifting away, catching with straight knees, rounding the back.
7) Regress: Do the movements separately. Progress: Start from the floor, increase load or use a complex (clean + front squat + jerk).

KMB-226.t: Front squat, hurdle jumps and 10 m sprint contrast
KMB-226.ht:
1) Setup: Prepare the equipment (Barbell, 4-5 hurdle, cone) so that transitions between movements are short.
2) Front squat: Feet shoulder-width apart, toes slightly out; load in a safe position, chest up, trunk braced. Send the hips back and down, knees tracking over the toes, and descend until the thighs are parallel (or to the lowest controlled position). Drive the whole foot into the floor and extend hips and knees together to return to the start.
3) Hurdle jumps: Athletic stance, feet hip-width. Jump maximally with a fast countermovement; hips-knees-ankles fully extend. Land softly on the balls of the feet, knees over the toes; stick 2 s if required.
4) 10 m sprint contrast: Take the start position (standing / falling / from the ground). On the cue run at maximal speed: short powerful first steps, trunk forward, active arms. Decelerate progressively after the distance; full rest between reps.
5) Transition: Move to the next movement within a few seconds; every part at maximal quality.
6) Dose: 3 x 1 round · %30-60 1RM / maximal · rest: 2-3 min. Stop the set if technique breaks.
7) Common mistakes: Pausing in the transition, doing the second movement poorly because of fatigue. Rounding the back, bending the knees too much (turning it into a squat), load drifting away from the legs, leaning back at the top.
8) Regress: Do the movements separately. Progress: Increase load, go single-leg or lower in 3-4 s.

KMB-227.t: Single-leg RDL to DB hang clean to reverse lunge
KMB-227.ht:
1) Setup: Prepare the equipment (2 dumbbell (8-16 kg)) so that transitions between movements are short.
2) Single-leg RDL: Feet hip-width, knees soft, load in front of the thighs; flat back, shoulders back. Push the hips back and hinge the trunk forward; the load stays close to the legs, hamstrings lengthen, back stays flat. Drive the hips forward and squeeze the glutes to stand tall; do not lean back from the lower back.
3) DB hang clean: Bar / dumbbells at mid-thigh or from the floor; arms straight, back flat. Extend hips-knees-ankles explosively, shrug, raise the load and drop under to catch if required. Lower the load under control; reduce the load if technique breaks.
4) Reverse lunge: Stand tall; load in the hands or on the shoulders, trunk upright. Step (forward / back / sideways) and lower under control until the front knee is about 90°, knee over the toes. Push through the front foot back to the start; equal reps on each leg.
5) Transition: Move to the next movement within a few seconds; every part at maximal quality. Equal reps on each leg / arm; start with the weaker side.
6) Dose: 3 x 4 / leg · %30-60 1RM / maximal · rest: 2-3 min. Stop the set if technique breaks.
7) Common mistakes: Pausing in the transition, doing the second movement poorly because of fatigue. Pulling the bar with the arms, bar drifting away, catching with straight knees, rounding the back.
8) Regress: Do the movements separately. Progress: Start from the floor, increase load or use a complex (clean + front squat + jerk).

KMB-228.ht:
1) Setup: Prepare the equipment (Landmine + plate) so that transitions between movements are short.
2) Landmine row: Trunk hinged or chest supported, arms straight. Pull the load to the chest/waist with elbows close to the body and squeeze the shoulder blades. Lower under control until the arms are fully extended.
3) Rotational press: Standing or kneeling, load at shoulder height, trunk braced. Press the load overhead until the arms are straight. Lower to the shoulders under control; do not arch the lower back.
4) Transition: Move to the next movement within a few seconds; every part at maximal quality. Equal reps on each leg / arm; start with the weaker side.
5) Dose: 3 x 6 / side · %30-60 1RM / maximal · rest: 2-3 min. Stop the set if technique breaks.
6) Common mistakes: Pausing in the transition, doing the second movement poorly because of fatigue. Arching the lower back, ribs flaring, pressing the load forward.
7) Regress: Do the movements separately. Progress: Increase load, single arm or standing push press.

KMB-229.ht:
1) Setup: Prepare the equipment (Kettlebell (8-20 kg)) so that transitions between movements are short.
2) Turkish get-up: Perform the movement from the correct start position, through full range and under control.
3) Windmill: Perform the movement from the correct start position, through full range and under control.
4) Transition: Move to the next movement within a few seconds; every part at maximal quality. Equal reps on each leg / arm; start with the weaker side.
5) Dose: 3 x 2 / side · RPE 7-8 · rest: 90 s. Stop the set if technique breaks.
6) Common mistakes: Pausing in the transition, doing the second movement poorly because of fatigue.
7) Regress: Do the movements separately. Progress: Increase load or add a third movement.

AE-01.ht:
1) Setup: Plank / dead bug / rollout position. Equipment: Bodyweight.
2) Execution: Keep the ribs down and the lower back neutral while moving arms and legs.
3) Return / finish: Do not let the lower back arch; do not hold your breath. Equal reps on each leg / arm; start with the weaker side.
4) Tempo and breathing: Controlled lowering, powerful and determined push / pull. (Tempo: 2-1-2.) Breathe out in the effort, in on the return; do not hold your breath for long.
5) Dose: 2-3 x 8-12 / 20-40 s · BW – light · rest: 30-45 s.
6) Common mistakes: Lower back arching, hips piking, holding the breath.
7) Regress: Kneeling or short lever. Progress: Longer lever (arms forward), more time or reps.

2) Execution: Keep the ribs down and the lower back neutral while moving arms and legs.
3) Return / finish: Do not let the lower back arch; do not hold your breath.
4) Tempo and breathing: Controlled lowering, powerful and determined push / pull. (Tempo: 2-1-2.) Breathe out in the effort, in on the return; do not hold your breath for long.
5) Dose: 2-3 x 8-12 / 20-40 s · BW – light · rest: 30-45 s.
6) Common mistakes: Lower back arching, hips piking, holding the breath.
7) Regress: Kneeling or short lever. Progress: Longer lever (arms forward), more time or reps.

CFE-32.t: Reverse crunch to knee-up with rotation
CFE-32.ht:
1) Setup: Prepare the equipment (Bench) so that transitions between movements are short.
2) Reverse crunch: Perform the movement from the correct start position, through full range and under control.
3) Knee-up with rotation: Perform the movement from the correct start position, through full range and under control.
4) Transition: Move to the next movement within a few seconds; every part at maximal quality.
5) Dose: 2-3 x 8-12 / 20-40 s · BW – light · rest: 30-45 s. Stop the set if technique breaks.
6) Common mistakes: Pausing in the transition, doing the second movement poorly because of fatigue. Pulling on the neck, using speed, arching the lower back.
7) Regress: Do the movements separately. Progress: Add load or slow the tempo.

DP-01.ht:
1) Setup: Athletic stance, feet hip-width. Equipment: Bodyweight.
2) Execution: Jump maximally with a fast countermovement; hips-knees-ankles fully extend.
3) Return / finish: Land softly on the balls of the feet, knees over the toes; stick 2 s if required.
4) Tempo and breathing: Move at maximal speed, explosively; short ground contact. Every rep high quality, no accumulated fatigue. Breathe out in the effort, in on the return; do not hold your breath for long.
5) Dose: 2-4 x 3-6 · Maximal · rest: 60-90 s.
6) Common mistakes: Hard noisy landings, knees caving in, long ground contacts (reactive drills), continuing when fatigued.
7) Regress: Lower the height, stick every rep. Progress: Increase height / distance, go single leg or continuous (reactive).

DP-54.ht:
1) Setup: Prepare the equipment (Box + hurdle) so that transitions between movements are short.
2) Derinlik: Perform the movement from the correct start position, through full range and under control.
3) Engel sıçrama (depth hurdle): Feet hip-width, knees soft, load in front of the thighs; flat back, shoulders back. Push the hips back and hinge the trunk forward; the load stays close to the legs, hamstrings lengthen, back stays flat. Drive the hips forward and squeeze the glutes to stand tall; do not lean back from the lower back.
4) Transition: Move to the next movement within a few seconds; every part at maximal quality.
5) Dose: 3 x 5 · BW – maximal · rest: 90-120 s. Stop the set if technique breaks.
6) Common mistakes: Pausing in the transition, doing the second movement poorly because of fatigue. Hard noisy landings, knees caving in, long ground contacts (reactive drills), continuing when fatigued.
7) Regress: Do the movements separately. Progress: Increase height / distance, go single leg or continuous (reactive).

DP-58.ht:
1) Setup: Prepare the equipment (Trap bar) so that transitions between movements are short.
2) Trap bar deadlift: Feet hip-width, knees soft, load in front of the thighs; flat back, shoulders back. Drive the hips forward and squeeze the glutes to stand tall; do not lean back from the lower back.

2) Execution: Complete the course as fast as possible, lowering the centre of mass at each change of direction.
3) Return / finish: Full rest; quality before speed. Equal reps on each leg / arm; start with the weaker side.
4) Tempo and breathing: Move at maximal speed, explosively; short ground contact. Every rep high quality, no accumulated fatigue. Breathe out in the effort, in on the return; do not hold your breath for long.
5) Dose: 3-4 x 4 · Maximal · rest: 90-120 s.
6) Common mistakes: Staying upright in turns, looking at the floor, long instead of short steps.
7) Regress: Reduce distance and speed, pre-planned course. Progress: Reactive (cue-based) change of direction, add a ball or opponent.

MT-41.ht:
1) Setup: Prepare the equipment (Med ball) so that transitions between movements are short.
2) Med ball slam: Ball at the chest / hip / overhead, athletic stance. Start from the legs and transfer force through hips and trunk to throw the ball as fast as possible. Catch or retrieve the ball; every rep at maximal speed.
3) Sprint: Take the start position (standing / falling / from the ground). On the cue run at maximal speed: short powerful first steps, trunk forward, active arms. Decelerate progressively after the distance; full rest between reps.
4) Transition: Move to the next movement within a few seconds; every part at maximal quality.
5) Dose: 4 x 1+10 m · %30-60 1RM / maximal · rest: 2-3 min. Stop the set if technique breaks.

7) Regress: Do the movements separately. Progress: Heavier ball, add a step or reactive (partner) throws.

MT-43.t: Contrast Bench press to med ball chest pass
MT-43.ht:
1) Setup: Prepare the equipment (Barbell) so that transitions between movements are short.

3) Med ball chest pass: Ball at the chest / hip / overhead, athletic stance. Start from the legs and transfer force through hips and trunk to throw the ball as fast as possible. Catch or retrieve the ball; every rep at maximal speed.

5) Dose: 3-4 x (3-5 + 3-5) · %30-60 1RM / maximal · rest: 2-3 min. Stop the set if technique breaks.
6) Common mistakes: Pausing in the transition, doing the second movement poorly because of fatigue. Waiting too long or not at all between the heavy and fast movement, fast movement losing quality.
7) Regress: Do the movements separately. Progress: Heavy load to 85%, make the fast movement reactive.

OL-46.t: Hang power clean to explosive step-up
OL-46.m: Gluteus, Quadriceps (+ Hamstring, Trapezius/Scapular, Gastrocnemius/Soleus, Deltoid)
OL-46.ht:
1) Setup: Prepare the equipment (Barbell + box (40 cm)) so that transitions between movements are short.
2) Hang power clean: Bar / dumbbells at mid-thigh or from the floor; arms straight, back flat. Extend hips-knees-ankles explosively, shrug, raise the load and drop under to catch if required. Lower the load under control; reduce the load if technique breaks.
3) Explosive step-up: Stand in front of the box with one foot on top (knee about 90°). Drive through the top foot and step fully onto the box; the back leg does not help. Lower under control (2-3 s); do not let the knee cave in.
4) Transition: Move to the next movement within a few seconds; every part at maximal quality. Equal reps on each leg / arm; start with the weaker side.
5) Dose: 4 x (2 clean + 2/leg step-up) · %60-80 1RM · rest: 2-3 min. Stop the set if technique breaks.
6) Common mistakes: Pausing in the transition, doing the second movement poorly because of fatigue. Pulling the bar with the arms, bar drifting away, catching with straight knees, rounding the back.
7) Regress: Do the movements separately. Progress: Start from the floor, increase load or use a complex (clean + front squat + jerk).

OL-49.t: Jump shrug to box jump complex
OL-49.ht:
1) Setup: Prepare the equipment (Barbell + box (50-60 cm)) so that transitions between movements are short.
2) Jump shrug: Hold the load with straight arms, stand tall. Lift the shoulders toward the ears, hold 1 s. Lower under control; elbows stay straight.
3) Box jump complex: Athletic stance, feet hip-width. Jump maximally with a fast countermovement; hips-knees-ankles fully extend. Land softly on the balls of the feet, knees over the toes; stick 2 s if required.
4) Transition: Move to the next movement within a few seconds; every part at maximal quality.
5) Dose: 4 x (3 + 3) · %60-80 1RM · rest: 2-3 min. Stop the set if technique breaks.
6) Common mistakes: Pausing in the transition, doing the second movement poorly because of fatigue. Pulling the bar with the arms, bar drifting away, catching with straight knees, rounding the back.
7) Regress: Do the movements separately. Progress: Start from the floor, increase load or use a complex (clean + front squat + jerk).

OL-50.t: Hang power snatch to overhead squat
OL-50.ht:
1) Setup: Prepare the equipment (Barbell (wide grip)) so that transitions between movements are short.
2) Hang power snatch: Bar / dumbbells at mid-thigh or from the floor; arms straight, back flat. Extend hips-knees-ankles explosively, shrug, raise the load and drop under to catch if required. Lower the load under control; reduce the load if technique breaks.
3) Overhead squat: Feet shoulder-width apart, toes slightly out; load in a safe position, chest up, trunk braced. Send the hips back and down, knees tracking over the toes, and descend until the thighs are parallel (or to the lowest controlled position). Drive the whole foot into the floor and extend hips and knees together to return to the start.
4) Transition: Move to the next movement within a few seconds; every part at maximal quality.
5) Dose: 4 x (2 + 1) · %60-80 1RM · rest: 2-3 min. Stop the set if technique breaks.
6) Common mistakes: Pausing in the transition, doing the second movement poorly because of fatigue. Pulling the bar with the arms, bar drifting away, catching with straight knees, rounding the back.

1) Setup: Heels fixed (partner / machine / strap), hips extended. Equipment: Partner / bank.
2) Execution: Bend the knee with the hamstrings (curl) or lower the trunk slowly forward (Nordic).
3) Return / finish: Make the eccentric part slow (3-5 s); do not bend at the hips.
4) Tempo and breathing: The lowering (lengthening) phase is slow and controlled; the return can be assisted or fast. Breathe out in the effort, in on the return; do not hold your breath for long.
5) Dose: 1 x 3 · BW · rest: 30 s.
6) Common mistakes: Bending at the hips, fast eccentric, arching the lower back.
7) Regress: Shorten the range, use band assistance. Progress: Longer eccentric, single leg or larger range.

HZ-46.ht:
1) Setup: Prepare the equipment (Wall) so that transitions between movements are short.
2) Tibialis: Perform the movement from the correct start position, through full range and under control.
3) Soleus isometric primer: Perform the movement from the correct start position, through full range and under control.
4) Transition: Move to the next movement within a few seconds; every part at maximal quality.
5) Dose: 1 x (30 s + 30 s) · BW · rest: 30 s. Stop the set if technique breaks.
6) Common mistakes: Pausing in the transition, doing the second movement poorly because of fatigue. Half range, bouncing, ankle rolling in / out.
7) Regress: Do the movements separately. Progress: Single leg, full range on a step or add load.

HZ-47.ht:
1) Setup: Prepare the equipment (Cone) so that transitions between movements are short.
2) A-skip: Athletic stance, feet hip-width. Jump maximally with a fast countermovement; hips-knees-ankles fully extend. Land softly on the balls of the feet, knees over the toes; stick 2 s if required.
3) B-skip: Athletic stance, feet hip-width. Jump maximally with a fast countermovement; hips-knees-ankles fully extend. Land softly on the balls of the feet, knees over the toes; stick 2 s if required.
4) Acceleration: Take the start position (standing / falling / from the ground). On the cue run at maximal speed: short powerful first steps, trunk forward, active arms. Decelerate progressively after the distance; full rest between reps.
5) Transition: Move to the next movement within a few seconds; every part at maximal quality.
6) Dose: 2 x (15 m + 15 m + 15 m) · BW · rest: 30 s. Stop the set if technique breaks.
7) Common mistakes: Pausing in the transition, doing the second movement poorly because of fatigue. Hard noisy landings, knees caving in, long ground contacts (reactive drills), continuing when fatigued.
8) Regress: Do the movements separately. Progress: Increase height / distance, go single leg or continuous (reactive).

HZ-48.ht:
1) Setup: Side-lying / side plank or standing band position. Equipment: Bodyweight.
2) Execution: Pull the leg toward the midline with the inner thigh or hold the position.
3) Return / finish: Release under control; do not rotate the pelvis. Equal reps on each leg / arm; start with the weaker side.
4) Tempo and breathing: Controlled lowering, powerful and determined push / pull. Breathe out in the effort, in on the return; do not hold your breath for long.
5) Dose: 1 x 8 / side · BW · rest: –.
6) Common mistakes: Pelvis dropping or rotating, holding the breath, forcing a painful range.
7) Regress: Short lever (knee bent). Progress: Long lever (knee straight), longer hold or dynamic version.

HZ-49.ht:
1) Setup: Prepare the equipment (Mini / long band) so that transitions between movements are short.
2) Bant pull-apart: Perform the movement from the correct start position, through full range and under control.
3) Dış rotasyon: Perform the movement from the correct start position, through full range and under control.
4) Transition: Move to the next movement within a few seconds; every part at maximal quality.
5) Dose: 1-2 x 12 · BW · rest: 30 s. Stop the set if technique breaks.
6) Common mistakes: Pausing in the transition, doing the second movement poorly because of fatigue. Swinging the trunk, shrugging, pulling with the body instead of the arms.
7) Regress: Do the movements separately. Progress: Single arm, 2 s hold at the top or more load.

HZ-50.ht:
1) Setup: Take the start position for the exercise; trunk tall and braced, joints neutral. Equipment: Bodyweight. Keep the straps taut; body angle sets the difficulty (more upright = easier).
2) Execution: Perform the movement under control and through full range.
3) Return / finish: Return to the start under control and prepare for the next rep. Equal reps on each leg / arm; start with the weaker side.
4) Tempo and breathing: Controlled lowering, powerful and determined push / pull. Breathe out in the effort, in on the return; do not hold your breath for long.
5) Dose: 1 x 10 / side · BW · rest: –.
6) Common mistakes: Rounding the back, bending the knees too much (turning it into a squat), load drifting away from the legs, leaning back at the top.
7) Regress: Shorten the range (just below the knee), learn the hinge with a dowel on the back. Progress: Increase load, go single-leg or lower in 3-4 s.

STB-10.t: Single-leg calf raise on balance pad
STB-10.ht:
1) Setup: Balls of the feet on a step, knees straight or bent (soleus). Equipment: Balance pedi. Work on one leg; keep the pelvis level and the stance knee over the toes.
2) Execution: Rise onto the toes as high as possible and hold 1 s.
3) Return / finish: Lower the heels slowly below the step. Equal reps on each leg / arm; start with the weaker side.
4) Tempo and breathing: Controlled lowering, powerful and determined push / pull. (Tempo: 2-1-2.) Breathe out in the effort, in on the return; do not hold your breath for long.
5) Dose: 2-3 x 10-12 / side · BW · rest: 30-45 s.
6) Common mistakes: Half range, bouncing, ankle rolling in / out.
7) Regress: Both feet on flat ground. Progress: Single leg, full range on a step or add load.

STB-11.ht:
1) Setup: Feet shoulder-width apart, toes slightly out; load in a safe position, chest up, trunk braced. Equipment: Balance pedi. Work on one leg; keep the pelvis level and the stance knee over the toes.
2) Execution: Send the hips back and down, knees tracking over the toes, and descend until the thighs are parallel (or to the lowest controlled position).
3) Return / finish: Drive the whole foot into the floor and extend hips and knees together to return to the start. Equal reps on each leg / arm; start with the weaker side.
4) Tempo and breathing: Controlled lowering, powerful and determined push / pull. (Tempo: 3-1-1.) Breathe out in the effort, in on the return; do not hold your breath for long.
5) Dose: 2-3 x 6-10 / side · BW – light load · rest: 45-60 s.
6) Common mistakes: Knees caving in, heels lifting, lower back rounding at the bottom, chest dropping.
7) Regress: Squat to a box or use a goblet position, reduce depth. Progress: Increase load, pause 2 s at the bottom or use a tempo squat (3 s down).

STB-18.ht:
1) Setup: Stand in front of the box with one foot on top (knee about 90°). Equipment: Cone.
2) Execution: Drive through the top foot and step fully onto the box; the back leg does not help.
3) Return / finish: Lower under control (2-3 s); do not let the knee cave in. Equal reps on each leg / arm; start with the weaker side.
4) Tempo and breathing: The lowering (lengthening) phase is slow and controlled; the return can be assisted or fast. Breathe out in the effort, in on the return; do not hold your breath for long.

STB-19.t: Lateral bound to stick on pad
STB-19.ht:
1) Setup: Athletic stance, feet hip-width. Equipment: Balance pedi. Movement is sideways (frontal plane); knee and toes point in the direction of travel.
2) Execution: Jump maximally with a fast countermovement; hips-knees-ankles fully extend.
3) Return / finish: Land softly on the balls of the feet, knees over the toes; stick 2 s if required. Equal reps on each leg / arm; start with the weaker side.
4) Tempo and breathing: Move at maximal speed, explosively; short ground contact. Every rep high quality, no accumulated fatigue. Breathe out in the effort, in on the return; do not hold your breath for long.
5) Dose: 2-3 x 4-6 / side (3 s stick) · Submaximal – quality landing · rest: 60 s.

7) Regress: Lower the height, stick every rep. Progress: Increase height / distance, go single leg or continuous (reactive).

STB-20.ht:
1) Setup: Feet hip-width, knees soft, load in front of the thighs; flat back, shoulders back. Equipment: Balance pedi + DB. Work on one leg; keep the pelvis level and the stance knee over the toes.
2) Execution: Push the hips back and hinge the trunk forward; the load stays close to the legs, hamstrings lengthen, back stays flat.
3) Return / finish: Drive the hips forward and squeeze the glutes to stand tall; do not lean back from the lower back. Equal reps on each leg / arm; start with the weaker side.
4) Tempo and breathing: Controlled lowering, powerful and determined push / pull. (Tempo: 2-1-2.) Breathe out in the effort, in on the return; do not hold your breath for long.
5) Dose: 2-3 x 8-10 / side · BW – light · rest: 45 s.
6) Common mistakes: Rounding the back, bending the knees too much (turning it into a squat), load drifting away from the legs, leaning back at the top.
7) Regress: Shorten the range (just below the knee), learn the hinge with a dowel on the back. Progress: Increase load, go single-leg or lower in 3-4 s.

STB-21.ht:
1) Setup: Lie on your back or with the upper back on a bench, feet on the floor, knees about 90°. Equipment: BOSU. Work on one leg; keep the pelvis level and the stance knee over the toes.
2) Execution: Drive through the heels and lift the hips until trunk and thighs form a straight line; squeeze the glutes.
3) Return / finish: Lower under control; do not arch the lower back. Equal reps on each leg / arm; start with the weaker side.
4) Tempo and breathing: Controlled lowering, powerful and determined push / pull. (Tempo: 2-1-2.) Breathe out in the effort, in on the return; do not hold your breath for long.
5) Dose: 2-3 x 8-10 / side · BW – light · rest: 45 s.
6) Common mistakes: Lifting from the lower back, not squeezing the glutes, knees opening / collapsing.
7) Regress: Reduce range, use both legs. Progress: Single leg, add load or hold 3 s at the top.

1) Setup: Feet shoulder-width apart, toes slightly out; load in a safe position, chest up, trunk braced. Equipment: Cable / band. Work on one leg; keep the pelvis level and the stance knee over the toes.
2) Execution: Send the hips back and down, knees tracking over the toes, and descend until the thighs are parallel (or to the lowest controlled position).
3) Return / finish: Drive the whole foot into the floor and extend hips and knees together to return to the start. Equal reps on each leg / arm; start with the weaker side.
4) Tempo and breathing: Position stays still; keep the force for the whole duration. Breathe rhythmically throughout; do not hold your breath.
5) Dose: 2-3 x 20-40 s / 8-10 reps · BW · rest: 30-45 s.
6) Common mistakes: Knees caving in, heels lifting, lower back rounding at the bottom, chest dropping.
7) Regress: Squat to a box or use a goblet position, reduce depth. Progress: Increase load, pause 2 s at the bottom or use a tempo squat (3 s down).

STB-30.ht:
1) Setup: Ball at the chest / hip / overhead, athletic stance. Equipment: Küçük ball. Perform with the ball; technical quality before speed.
2) Execution: Start from the legs and transfer force through hips and trunk to throw the ball as fast as possible.
3) Return / finish: Catch or retrieve the ball; every rep at maximal speed. Equal reps on each leg / arm; start with the weaker side.
4) Tempo and breathing: Move at maximal speed, explosively; short ground contact. Every rep high quality, no accumulated fatigue. Breathe out in the effort, in on the return; do not hold your breath for long.
5) Dose: 2-3 x 20-30 s / 8-12 reps · BW – light · rest: 30-45 s.
6) Common mistakes: Throwing with the arms only, no hip drive, over-arching the back.
7) Regress: Lighter ball, throw from a static position. Progress: Heavier ball, add a step or reactive (partner) throws.

STB-31.ht:

4) Tempo and breathing: Position stays still; keep the force for the whole duration. Breathe rhythmically throughout; do not hold your breath.
5) Dose: 2-3 x 20-30 s / 8-12 reps · BW – light · rest: 30-45 s.
6) Common mistakes: Hips lifting off the seat, dropping the load, working in a painful range.
7) Regress: Reduce load, limit range to pain-free. Progress: Hold 2-3 s at the top, longer eccentric or single leg.

STB-32.ht:

3) Return / finish: Press powerfully with chest and arms; elbows about 45°.
4) Tempo and breathing: Controlled lowering, powerful and determined push / pull. Breathe out in the effort, in on the return; do not hold your breath for long.
5) Dose: 2-3 x 20-30 s / 8-12 reps · BW – light · rest: 30-45 s.
6) Common mistakes: Elbows flaring 90°, hips sagging (push-up), bouncing the bar, shoulders rolling forward.
7) Regress: Incline push-up or light dumbbells. Progress: Increase load, tempo (3 s down) or single-arm version.

2) Execution: Brake from the given entry speed with progressive steps; on the last step hips back, trunk slightly forward.
3) Return / finish: Hold the position 2-3 s (stick); knee over the toes. Equal reps on each leg / arm; start with the weaker side.

6) Common mistakes: Single hard braking step, trunk leaning back, knee caving in.
7) Regress: Lower entry speed, longer braking distance. Progress: Higher entry speed, shorter braking distance, add a change of direction.

DEC-28.ht:
1) Setup: Feet shoulder-width apart, toes slightly out; load in a safe position, chest up, trunk braced. Equipment: Flywheel (kBox) + yan bağlantı. Make the lowering (eccentric) phase slow (3-5 s). Movement is sideways (frontal plane); knee and toes point in the direction of travel.
2) Execution: Send the hips back and down, knees tracking over the toes, and descend until the thighs are parallel (or to the lowest controlled position).
3) Return / finish: Drive the whole foot into the floor and extend hips and knees together to return to the start. Equal reps on each leg / arm; start with the weaker side.
4) Tempo and breathing: The lowering (lengthening) phase is slow and controlled; the return can be assisted or fast. Breathe out in the effort, in on the return; do not hold your breath for long.
5) Dose: 3 x 6-8 / side · Eksantrik 3-5 s · rest: 90 s.
6) Common mistakes: Knees caving in, heels lifting, lower back rounding at the bottom, chest dropping.
7) Regress: Squat to a box or use a goblet position, reduce depth. Progress: Increase load, pause 2 s at the bottom or use a tempo squat (3 s down).

3) Return / finish: Push through the front foot back to the start; equal reps on each leg. Equal reps on each leg / arm; start with the weaker side.

7) Regress: Static split squat, one hand on the wall for support. Progress: Increase load, elevate the rear foot (Bulgarian) or go walking.

RHB-01.sr: 3 x 10 x 5-10 s squeeze, per day 2-3
RHB-01.ht:
1) Setup: On a machine or in an isometric position, back supported. Equipment: Towel / rulo. On sliders / a towel; keep hips up and controlled throughout the slide.
2) Execution: Extend the knee under control and hold 1 s at the top.
3) Return / finish: Lower slowly. Equal reps on each leg / arm; start with the weaker side.
4) Tempo and breathing: Position stays still; keep the force for the whole duration. Breathe rhythmically throughout; do not hold your breath.
5) Dose: 3 x 10 x 5-10 s squeeze, per day 2-3 · rest: 10 s.
6) Common mistakes: Hips lifting off the seat, dropping the load, working in a painful range.
7) Regress: Reduce load, limit range to pain-free. Progress: Hold 2-3 s at the top, longer eccentric or single leg.

RHB-02.ht:
1) Setup: Light load, standing or lying prone. Equipment: Bodyweight / ayak bileği ağırlığı.
2) Execution: Raise the arm in the given direction; shoulder-blade control first.
3) Return / finish: Lower slowly. Equal reps on each leg / arm; start with the weaker side.
4) Tempo and breathing: Controlled lowering, powerful and determined push / pull. Breathe out in the effort, in on the return; do not hold your breath for long.
5) Dose: 3 x 10-15 · rest: 30 s.
6) Common mistakes: Shrugging, using momentum, choosing a heavy load.
7) Regress: Reduce load and range. Progress: Increase reps or hold time, add band resistance.

5) Dose: 2-3 x 10-15.
6) Common mistakes: Continuing with broken technique, moving fast and uncontrolled, working in a painful range.
7) Regress: Reduce load or range, use support. Progress: Progressively increase load, reps or time.

7) Regress: Squat to a box or use a goblet position, reduce depth. Progress: Increase load, pause 2 s at the bottom or use a tempo squat (3 s down).

RHB-120.ht:
1) Setup: Adjust the equipment to your body (seat height, belt speed etc.); warm up 3-5 min easy. Equipment: Field · cone · ball.
2) Execution: Work rhythmically for the given time and intensity; pain must stay ≤3/10.
3) Return / finish: Cool down by reducing intensity over the last 2-3 min.
4) Tempo and breathing: Rhythmic and controlled; start at a conversational pace and build up. Breathe out in the effort, in on the return; do not hold your breath for long.
5) Dose: 6-10 x (1 min jog + 1 min walk) · rest: –.
6) Common mistakes: Wrong equipment setup, increasing time despite pain, high intensity without warm-up.
7) Regress: Reduce time or resistance, use intervals (e.g. 1 min work – 1 min easy). Progress: Progressively increase time, resistance or interval intensity.

RHB-121.i: %60-70 Vmaks · İlerleme: Tek leg calf raise ≥20, SEBT farkı <4 cm sağlanınca bir sonraki steps.
RHB-121.rs: Between reps walk 30-45 s, between sets 2 min
RHB-121.ht:
1) Setup: Field / cones set up, warm-up done. Equipment: Field · cone · ball. Count the tempo (e.g. 3 s down, 1 s pause, controlled up). Perform with the ball; technical quality before speed.
2) Execution: Start at low intensity; distance, duration and speed progress according to pain and quality.
3) Return / finish: Do not progress before criteria are met (pain ≤3/10, no swelling next day).
4) Tempo and breathing: Controlled lowering, powerful and determined push / pull. Breathe out in the effort, in on the return; do not hold your breath for long.
5) Dose: 2 x 6-8 x 60-100 m · rest: Between reps walk 30-45 s, between sets 2 min.
6) Common mistakes: Progressing despite pain, ignoring next-day response.
7) Regress: Return to the previous level. Progress: Add speed / distance / change of direction once criteria are met.

RHB-152.ht:

TST-01.sr: Warm-up: 5-10 reps 40-60% → 3-5 reps 60-80% → 2-3 reps 80-90% → reach 1RM in 3-5 attempts (NSCA)
TST-01.ht:
1) Setup: Feet shoulder-width apart, toes slightly out; load in a safe position, chest up, trunk braced. Equipment: Barbell + rack.
2) Execution: Send the hips back and down, knees tracking over the toes, and descend until the thighs are parallel (or to the lowest controlled position).
3) Return / finish: Drive the whole foot into the floor and extend hips and knees together to return to the start.
4) Tempo and breathing: Controlled lowering, powerful and determined push / pull. Breathe out in the effort, in on the return; do not hold your breath for long.
5) Dose: Warm-up: 5-10 reps 40-60% → 3-5 reps 60-80% → 2-3 reps 80-90% → reach 1RM in 3-5 attempts (NSCA) · 1RM (kg) · relative 1RM (kg/kg) · rest: 3-5 min between attempts.
6) Common mistakes: Knees caving in, heels lifting, lower back rounding at the bottom, chest dropping.
7) Regress: Squat to a box or use a goblet position, reduce depth. Progress: Increase load, pause 2 s at the bottom or use a tempo squat (3 s down).

TST-02.sr: Warm-up: 5-10 reps 40-60% → 3-5 reps 60-80% → 2-3 reps 80-90% → reach 1RM in 3-5 attempts (NSCA)
TST-02.ht:
1) Setup: Feet shoulder-width apart, toes slightly out; load in a safe position, chest up, trunk braced. Equipment: Barbell + bench. Box / bench must be stable and non-slip; choose the height by level.
2) Execution: Send the hips back and down, knees tracking over the toes, and descend until the thighs are parallel (or to the lowest controlled position).
3) Return / finish: Drive the whole foot into the floor and extend hips and knees together to return to the start.
4) Tempo and breathing: Controlled lowering, powerful and determined push / pull. Breathe out in the effort, in on the return; do not hold your breath for long.
5) Dose: Warm-up: 5-10 reps 40-60% → 3-5 reps 60-80% → 2-3 reps 80-90% → reach 1RM in 3-5 attempts (NSCA) · 1RM (kg) · relative 1RM (kg/kg) · rest: 3-5 min between attempts.
6) Common mistakes: Knees caving in, heels lifting, lower back rounding at the bottom, chest dropping.
7) Regress: Squat to a box or use a goblet position, reduce depth. Progress: Increase load, pause 2 s at the bottom or use a tempo squat (3 s down).

TST-03.sr: Warm-up: 5-10 reps 40-60% → 3-5 reps 60-80% → 2-3 reps 80-90% → reach 1RM in 3-5 attempts (NSCA)
TST-03.ht:
1) Setup: Feet hip-width, knees soft, load in front of the thighs; flat back, shoulders back. Equipment: Barbell / trap bar.
2) Execution: Push the hips back and hinge the trunk forward; the load stays close to the legs, hamstrings lengthen, back stays flat.
3) Return / finish: Drive the hips forward and squeeze the glutes to stand tall; do not lean back from the lower back.
4) Tempo and breathing: Controlled lowering, powerful and determined push / pull. Breathe out in the effort, in on the return; do not hold your breath for long.
5) Dose: Warm-up: 5-10 reps 40-60% → 3-5 reps 60-80% → 2-3 reps 80-90% → reach 1RM in 3-5 attempts (NSCA) · 1RM (kg) · relative 1RM (kg/kg) · rest: 3-5 min between attempts.
6) Common mistakes: Rounding the back, bending the knees too much (turning it into a squat), load drifting away from the legs, leaning back at the top.
7) Regress: Shorten the range (just below the knee), learn the hinge with a dowel on the back. Progress: Increase load, go single-leg or lower in 3-4 s.

TST-04.sr: Warm-up: 5-10 reps 40-60% → 3-5 reps 60-80% → 2-3 reps 80-90% → reach 1RM in 3-5 attempts (NSCA)
TST-04.ht:
1) Setup: Bar / dumbbells at mid-thigh or from the floor; arms straight, back flat. Equipment: Barbell.
2) Execution: Extend hips-knees-ankles explosively, shrug, raise the load and drop under to catch if required.
3) Return / finish: Lower the load under control; reduce the load if technique breaks.
4) Tempo and breathing: Move at maximal speed, explosively; short ground contact. Every rep high quality, no accumulated fatigue. Breathe out in the effort, in on the return; do not hold your breath for long.
5) Dose: Warm-up: 5-10 reps 40-60% → 3-5 reps 60-80% → 2-3 reps 80-90% → reach 1RM in 3-5 attempts (NSCA) · 1RM (kg) · relative 1RM (kg/kg) · rest: 3-5 min between attempts.
6) Common mistakes: Pulling the bar with the arms, bar drifting away, catching with straight knees, rounding the back.
7) Regress: Start from the hang with a light load; teach with jump shrug / high pull. Progress: Start from the floor, increase load or use a complex (clean + front squat + jerk).

TST-05.sr: Warm-up: 5-10 reps 40-60% → 3-5 reps 60-80% → 2-3 reps 80-90% → reach 1RM in 3-5 attempts (NSCA)
TST-05.ht:
1) Setup: Lie on your back or with the upper back on a bench, feet on the floor, knees about 90°. Equipment: Barbell + bench.
2) Execution: Drive through the heels and lift the hips until trunk and thighs form a straight line; squeeze the glutes.
3) Return / finish: Lower under control; do not arch the lower back.
4) Tempo and breathing: Controlled lowering, powerful and determined push / pull. Breathe out in the effort, in on the return; do not hold your breath for long.
5) Dose: Warm-up: 5-10 reps 40-60% → 3-5 reps 60-80% → 2-3 reps 80-90% → reach 1RM in 3-5 attempts (NSCA) · 1RM (kg) · relative 1RM (kg/kg) · rest: 3-5 min between attempts.
6) Common mistakes: Lifting from the lower back, not squeezing the glutes, knees opening / collapsing.
7) Regress: Reduce range, use both legs. Progress: Single leg, add load or hold 3 s at the top.

TST-10.sr: Find the max load for 3-5 reps; Brzycki: 1RM = load / (1.0278 − 0.0278 × reps)

2) 3-5RM testi: Perform the movement from the correct start position, through full range and under control.
3) 1RM tahmini (Brzycki / Epley): Perform the movement from the correct start position, through full range and under control.
4) Transition: Move to the next movement within a few seconds; every part at maximal quality.
5) Dose: Find the max load for 3-5 reps; Brzycki: 1RM = load / (1.0278 − 0.0278 × reps) · Estimated 1RM (kg) · rest: 3-5 min between attempts. Stop the set if technique breaks.
6) Common mistakes: Pausing in the transition, doing the second movement poorly because of fatigue. Continuing with broken technique, moving fast and uncontrolled, working in a painful range.
7) Regress: Do the movements separately. Progress: Progressively increase load, reps or time.

TST-26.sr: 1 x 3 maximal Nordic reps, slow lowering

TST-26.ht:
1) Setup: Heels fixed (partner / machine / strap), hips extended. Equipment: NordBord / Nordic device. Keep the straps taut; body angle sets the difficulty (more upright = easier).
2) Execution: Bend the knee with the hamstrings (curl) or lower the trunk slowly forward (Nordic).
3) Return / finish: Make the eccentric part slow (3-5 s); do not bend at the hips.
4) Tempo and breathing: The lowering (lengthening) phase is slow and controlled; the return can be assisted or fast. Breathe out in the effort, in on the return; do not hold your breath for long.

5) Dose: 3-5 maximal concentric flexion-extension at each velocity, L/R · Peak torque (N·m, N·m/kg) · conventional H:Q (≥0.6) · asymmetry % · rest: 60-90 s between velocities.
6) Common mistakes: Continuing with broken technique, moving fast and uncontrolled, working in a painful range.
7) Regress: Reduce load or range, use support. Progress: Progressively increase load, reps or time.

TST-31.ht:
1) Setup: Athletic stance, feet hip-width. Equipment: Force plate / My Jump / temas mat.
2) Execution: Jump maximally with a fast countermovement; hips-knees-ankles fully extend.
3) Return / finish: Land softly on the balls of the feet, knees over the toes; stick 2 s if required.
4) Tempo and breathing: Move at maximal speed, explosively; short ground contact. Every rep high quality, no accumulated fatigue. Breathe out in the effort, in on the return; do not hold your breath for long.
5) Dose: 3 maximal jumps, hands on hips, self-selected depth · Height (cm) · peak power (W/kg) · RSImod · eccentric/concentric impulse · rest: 30-60 s between jumps.
6) Common mistakes: Hard noisy landings, knees caving in, long ground contacts (reactive drills), continuing when fatigued.
7) Regress: Lower the height, stick every rep. Progress: Increase height / distance, go single leg or continuous (reactive).

2) Squat jump (SJ): Feet shoulder-width apart, toes slightly out; load in a safe position, chest up, trunk braced. Send the hips back and down, knees tracking over the toes, and descend until the thighs are parallel (or to the lowest controlled position). Drive the whole foot into the floor and extend hips and knees together to return to the start.
3) Eccentric utilisation ratio: Perform the movement from the correct start position, through full range and under control.
4) Transition: Move to the next movement within a few seconds; every part at maximal quality.
5) Dose: Hold 90° knee 2-3 s, 3 maximal jumps without countermovement · SJ height (cm) · EUR = CMJ/SJ · rest: 30-60 s. Stop the set if technique breaks.
6) Common mistakes: Pausing in the transition, doing the second movement poorly because of fatigue. Hard noisy landings, knees caving in, long ground contacts (reactive drills), continuing when fatigued.
7) Regress: Do the movements separately. Progress: Increase height / distance, go single leg or continuous (reactive).
